done_when: Every review removes its forge-review-* folder and the git worktree registration it created, including when the review fails, is interrupted (Ctrl-C or the process killed and run again) or the worktree removal fails; and each review first deletes forge-review-* folders older than a day that no running review owns. A command-level test interrupts a review and shows its folder is gone afterwards, and another shows an old leftover folder is removed by the next review.

findings.body: Concurrent review startup can lose ownership protection. Review A creates its lock at line 449 but has not yet locked it. Review B opens that lock, acquires it, and closes the handle at line 438, releasing it before deletion. A can then acquire the lock and create its review folder; B subsequently deletes that active folder at line 441. Alternatively, B unlinks the lock before A creates the folder, leaving A holding an unlinked lock; if A is killed, the next review leaves its fresh folder behind until it ages past a day. Synchronize lock publication with collection, retain the collector's lock through deletion, and handle failed ownership acquisition. The command-level tests do not exercise concurrent ownership, so they miss this acceptance-criterion failure.
